items.claim: Claude Haiku 5.5 API pricing is $0.10 input and $0.50 output per million tokens for prompts up to 100K tokens, and $0.50/$2.50 above that. Haiku 4.5 costs $1/$5.
items.why_it_matters: For short prompts that is 90% cheaper than Haiku 4.5, which changes the cost of high-volume classification and sub-agent calls.
items.try_this: Check how long your typical Haiku prompts are against the 100K-token price break before switching.

verification.method: Anthropic pricing page lists both Haiku 5.5 tiers and the Haiku 4.5 price

items.claim: Gemini 4 Argon (gemini-4-argon) is on the paid Gemini API at intro prices of $2 input and $10 output per million tokens until November 30, 2026. From December 1 the prices are $4 and $20.
items.why_it_matters: The price doubles after the intro period, so cost estimates for anything built now should use the December prices.
items.try_this: Use the December 1 prices of $4/$20 per million tokens when you budget Gemini 4 Argon workloads.

verification.method: Gemini API pricing page; the 1M output-limit claim was not confirmed there and is left out

items.claim: Meta released open weights for Muse Spark Open, an 816B-total, 42B-active MoE with 1M context and text, image, video and audio input. Its license requires 'Built with Muse Spark Open' attribution and a separate deal for model-as-a-service businesses with over $20M revenue.
items.why_it_matters: A large US open-weight multimodal model, but its license terms are stricter than Apache or MIT.
items.try_this: Read the Muse Model License on the model card before you build a product on it.

verification.method: Hugging Face model card confirms specs and license terms; benchmark numbers left out as vendor claims

items.claim: Reflection released Beam 1.0, a 501B-total, 23B-active MoE with 1M context, under Apache 2.0. It comes in BF16, FP8 and NVFP4 weights and has a published safety report.
items.why_it_matters: A large open model under a permissive license, which is simpler for commercial use than custom model licenses.
items.try_this: Compare the Apache 2.0 license on Beam's model card with the license of the open model you currently use.

verification.method: Hugging Face model card shows size, license and precisions; DFlash2 and Mirror CLI not confirmed there

items.claim: StepFun released Step-5-Preview open weights, a 600B-total, 27B-active MoE with up to 1M context. It uses the StepFun Model License 1.0, which adds attribution and commercial-license conditions, not plain Apache 2.0.
items.why_it_matters: Earlier StepFun models were Apache 2.0, so check the new license terms before using this one commercially.
items.try_this: Read the StepFun Model License 1.0 terms on the model card before commercial use.

verification.method: Hugging Face model card confirms size, context and license; the leak claim from Reddit commenters is unverified and left out

items.claim: Addy Osmani, Morgan Westlee Lunt and Qing Wang describe how the Claude Code team reviews code. Claude reviews every change continuously, other agents verify its findings before they are posted, and human approval depends on how risky the change is.
items.why_it_matters: It is a written, detailed review pipeline for teams where agents write most of the code, including when a human still has to approve.
items.try_this: Read the post's section on risk-based approval, then write down which paths in your repo should always need a human reviewer.

verification.method: Read the original claude.dev post (Oct 15, 2026); authors and review flow match the quote

items.excerpt: Now, review runs continuously, more like spellcheck while you write.

items.claim: Claude Code 2.1.300 gzips large requests to api.anthropic.com, even when telemetry is turned off. Setting CLAUDE_CODE_GZIP_REQUEST_BODIES=0 disables it.
items.why_it_matters: Smaller request bodies can cut latency on long sessions. The setting matters if a proxy or gateway rejects compressed bodies.
items.try_this: If you route Claude Code through a proxy and requests start failing after upgrading, try CLAUDE_CODE_GZIP_REQUEST_BODIES=0.

verification.method: Found the changelog entry under version 2.1.300; not tested hands-on

items.claim: A Gemini CLI change merged Oct 16, 2026 (PR #29774) adds a README note that the CLI is not optimized for Gemini 4 Argon. The PR's bot summary says the note points users to the Antigravity CLI.
items.why_it_matters: If you use Gemini 4 Argon from the terminal, Google itself says Gemini CLI may not be the right tool.
items.try_this: If you plan to use Gemini 4 Argon from the terminal, read the updated Gemini CLI README first.

verification.method: Merged PR page and nightly release notes; exact banner wording not visible, Antigravity pointer only in bot summary

items.claim: Gemini CLI nightly v0.66.0-nightly.20261017 accepts a 'keys' array in keybindings.json, passes termination signals from the bootstrap parent to the child process, and checks that a binary update is actually the one on PATH.
items.why_it_matters: These are small reliability fixes for people who script or customize Gemini CLI. They are nightly builds, not stable.

verification.method: GitHub release notes in snapshot list PRs #29773, #29790, #29757; not tested
verification.audit_note: Release notes list PRs #29773 (keys array in keybindings.json), #29790 (forward termination signals to child), #29757 (verify active binary on PATH).
